the photo-responsive bis(crowns) with azo linkages can be applied to the photo-control of the selective ion extraction.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of photo-responsive crown ethers and their applications for selective extraction and transport of alkali metal ions.
the design and synthesis of new photo-responsive crown ethers and their applications to photo-controlled ion-extraction, molecular recognition, etc.
the development of photo-responsive bis(crowns) for photo-regulated selective ion-extraction and photo-switchable ionophores for photo-regulated ion-selective electrode.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the results of the present work demonstrate that the photo-isomerization of the bis(crown ether)(I) is an effective means of controlling the selectivity of alkali metal cations in solvent extraction.

the photo-responsive bis(crowns) (I) and (II) have been shown to exhibit photo-controlled ion-selectivity, and that the photo-controlled ion-selectivities of (I) and of (II) are complementary to each other.
the photo-responsive bis(crowns) (I) and (II) are capable of selectively extracting alkali metal cations in the presence of a large excess of the corresponding alkali metal salts.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the photo-control of ion-selective extraction has been achieved by a bis(crown ether).
photo-control of selective alkali metal cation extraction can be achieved with photo-responsive bis(crowns).
the photo-isomerization of (I) from trans- to cis- form is accompanied with a remarkable change in the ion-extraction behavior.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the selectivity for Na+ and K+ is controlled by the cis-trans isomerization of the azo-linkage in bis(crown ether).
the selectivity of the photo-responsive bis(crowned ether) for alkali metal cations is determined by the relative affinity for the cations of the two photo-isomers of the bis(crowned ether).
